chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) addressed the women, so he said: 'O group of women! Give charity, and even if it is from your ornaments, and even if it is with a date, and even if it is a part of a date, for the majority of you would be the fuel of Hell, for you frequently curse and are ungrateful to your spouses.'

So a woman from the Clan of Suleym, who possessed intellect, said: 'O Messenger of Allah! Are we not the mothers, the carriers, the breast-feeders? Are there not from us, the daughters who stay (with their husbands), and the sisters who are kind?' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was moved emotionally and said to her: 'Childbearing, birth-giving, breast-feeders, merciful ones, if only they do not bring to their husbands what would make them arrive to the Fire.'
ai.seo_question: What is the reason given for women being the fuel of Hell and how is it resolved?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the dialectic between general spiritual warnings and specific merit in Shia tradition, where the Prophet’s initial warning about women being 'fuel of Hell' is nuanced by a learned woman from Banu Suleym who highlights their domestic virtues. The Prophet’s response clarifies that while their roles as mothers and wives are highly rewarded, the specific condition of not bringing their husbands into Hell through their conduct (often interpreted as obedience or influence) remains crucial. This reflects the Shia emphasis on the interplay between female agency, marital harmony, and spiritual accountability.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> addressed the women, so he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘O group of women! Give charity, and even if it is from your ornaments, and even if it is with a date, and even if it is a part of a date, for the majority of you would be the fuel of the Fire if you frequently abuse and curse your associate (husband)’.

So a woman from the Clan of Suleym for whom was intellect, said, ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! Are we not the mothers, the carriers, the breast-feeders. Are there not from us, the daughters who stay (with their husbands), and the sisters who are kind?’ So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> was moved emotionally and said to her: ‘Childbearing, birth giving, breast-feeders, merciful ones, if only they do not bring to their husbands what would make them arrive to the Fire’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Ali ibn abu Hamzah from abu Basir who has said the following:

“I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying that once the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, gave a speech for women and said, ‘O the community of women, you must give charity even if it is from your jewelries, a date or a piece of a date because the majority of you will be the fuel for the fire of hell if you frequently abuse and curse your associate (husband).’

A woman from banu Salim who had reason said, ‘O Messenger of Allah, we are mothers, who carry in our wombs and breastfeed. From us are daughters who highly value (parents and relatives) and kind sisters.’ The Messenger of Allah was moved emotionally and said, ‘Childbearing, birth-giving, breastfeeding and kindhearted ones, only if they do not bring to their husband’s (bed) something that will make them to feel the heat of fire (due to involving themselves in indecent acts).”’
